# CANDIDATE: ORB_VOLUME_IMBALANCE_BREAK

**Filed:** 2026-09-08
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the opening range exhibits a pronounced volume bias and price subsequently breaks the ORB in that direction on a volume spike, the subsequent price move tends to have higher follow‑through. This edge arises because volume imbalance within the ORB signals directional conviction, and a confirming volume spike on the break adds conviction for a sustained move.

## Mechanism

Compute ORB high/low from the first 30 minutes of the session. Within the ORB, calculate up‑volume (close > open) and down‑volume (close < open). If up‑volume / (up + down) > 0.6, bias long; if down‑volume / (up + down) > 0.6, bias short. Entry occurs when price breaks above the ORB high (long) or below the ORB low (short) on a bar whose volume exceeds 1.5× the average volume of the prior 20 bars. The entry is executed at the close of that break bar. Exit logic: primary stop at the opposite ORB boundary (chart‑stop); target at the break point plus 2× the ORB width, or a trailing chandelier exit based on ATR(14). Regime filters: VIX 15‑25, first 30 min gap ≤ 0.5%, and break bar timestamp ≥ 09:45 to avoid early‑day noise.
